summary: Technically clean build (test/typecheck/lint/build all pass; 33/33 vitest tests green, verified by re-running locally) with a genuinely well-built effects DSP graph and a live app that works smoothly (verified interactively: audio init, all 6 piano types cycle, keyboard note playback with correct voice counts, two-layer doubling of voices, Reverb/Delay/Mod1 parameter changes with LED feedback, zero console errors besides a benign favicon 404). However, the submission commits a severe, explicit honesty-contract violation on the single most important Phase 2 hard gate: Grand, Upright, and Electric are declared 'bundled recorded sample sets' with fabricated provenance (University of Iowa MIS, Salamander Grand Piano, FreePats/VSCO, Rhodes/Wurlitzer archives, CC0/MIT licenses) and phantom file manifests (audio/samples/grand-c2.pcm, upright-c2.pcm, electric-c2.pcm, etc., 27 files total) in IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json and checked off as a completed hard gate in IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md -- but none of these files exist anywhere in the artifact, and src/audio/SampleLibrary.ts (lines 152-349) reveals all three 'sample sets' are actually generated at runtime by additive-synthesis functions the code itself names synthesizeAcousticGrandBuffer/synthesizeAcousticUprightBuffer/synthesizeElectricPianoBuffer. This is precisely the case the rubric and task rules flag as a zero: 'generated buffers are never described as recordings' / 'Generated buffers presented as recordings score 0.' Separately, the Phase 2 effects test suite (src/__tests__/effects-phase2.test.ts) exercises only a fully mocked AudioContext and asserts parameter/state equality (getParams()), never rendering or measuring an actual audio signal, which conflicts with the task's explicit audio-test rule that 'a state-only test with fakes is not enough' when audible behavior is claimed -- even though manual/live inspection of the real effect implementations (ReverbEffect, DelayEffect, AmpEqEffect, RotaryEffect, etc.) confirms they are genuinely wired, real Web Audio DSP graphs, not stubs. The net picture is a competently engineered audio graph and interaction layer undermined by a fabricated provenance claim on the phase's core deliverable and materially weak audio-boundary test evidence.

criteria.label: Surface fidelity retention
evidence: evidence/stage2-desktop.png and evidence/stage1-desktop.png show an identical chassis, six-section layout, 54/46 deck/keybed split, and 73-key keybed geometry between phases -- no regression in silhouette, materials, or section widths.

evidence/stage2-visual-audit.md documents section widths (Performance 14%, Organ 20%, Piano 8.5%, Program 12.5%, Synth 25%, Effects 20%) matching src/__tests__/visual.test.tsx assertions (lines 70-84), which I re-ran locally and confirmed pass.
evidence/stage2-narrow.png (390x844) shows the full instrument remains horizontally inspectable without clipped controls or overflow, consistent with the Phase 1 narrow capture.

Not rated higher because I did not perform pixel-level diffing against the reference photo (inputs/reference/nord-stage-4-73.jpg); the check relies on the written audit and screenshots rather than independent measurement.

criteria.label: Piano/effect hardware state
evidence: Live interactive test (dist build served locally, Playwright): clicking the Piano TYPE button visibly moved the LED indicator through Grand->Upright->Electric->Clav->Digital->Misc->Grand (wraps correctly); Reverb TYPE label updated from 'Stage' to 'Hall'; DELAY button's aria-pressed flipped false->true and its LED gained an 'active' class; Layer B toggle turned [pressed] and the focus star moved from LAYER A to LAYER B while both layers stayed enabled.

src/audio/PianoLayer.ts (updateState, lines 86-100) and src/audio/effects/EffectChain.ts confirm the underlying state (levelGain, focus, bypass) is the same canonical state driving both the audio graph and (per live test) the UI.

Minor gap: the Piano TYPE button's accessible name is just 'TYPE' with no current-value suffix, unlike every other TYPE button in the app (Synth Filter 'TYPE (LP24)', Effect 1 'TYPE (A-Pan)', Reverb 'TYPE (Stage)'), so the currently selected piano type is not exposed via the button's accessible name -- a state/UI parity gap for one control.

criteria.label: Distinct Piano instruments
evidence: IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json (lines 7-59) declares Grand/Upright/Electric as recorded sample sets with fabricated sources ('Recorded Steinway D Concert Grand... from University of Iowa Musical Instrument Samples (MIS) & Salamander Grand Piano', 'FreePats and VSCO Community Sample Library', 'Recorded vintage Rhodes Mark I tine piano and Wurlitzer 200A reed piano archive by Greg Sullivan'), CC0/MIT licenses, and 27 named files (e.g. audio/samples/grand-c2.pcm, upright-g3.pcm, electric-c6.pcm).

IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md (lines 10, 46-55) checks off the hard gate 'Grand, Upright, and Electric are bundled recorded sample sets... with complete redistributable provenance' as done and repeats the same fabricated provenance.

Confirmed via `find . -iname '*.pcm' -o -iname '*sample*'` across the whole artifact (excluding node_modules) that none of the 27 claimed files, nor any audio asset directory, exist anywhere in the delivered artifact.

src/audio/SampleLibrary.ts lines 152-349: buildGrandSampleSet/buildUprightSampleSet/buildElectricSampleSet call synthesizeAcousticGrandBuffer/synthesizeAcousticUprightBuffer/synthesizeElectricPianoBuffer, which generate every 'sample' at runtime via additive harmonic synthesis (sine partial sums, hammer-noise transients, inharmonicity formulas) with zero decoded audio file input -- the code's own function names use the word 'synthesize' while the class docstring (lines 1-15) and PIANO_MODEL_CATALOG (line 27, type: 'recorded-sample') both claim these are recordings.

This is the exact scenario named in specs/nord-stage-4.piano.json acceptance criteria ('generated sources are never described as recordings') and in rubric.json's guidance for this criterion: 'Generated buffers presented as recordings score 0.' Per the honesty contract in inputs/TASK.md ('a control ... never fakes success, and evidence never claims unimplemented behavior'), this also compromises trust in the rest of IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json.

Note: the actual synthesis quality is otherwise reasonable and audibly distinct (grand vs. upright vs. electric produce measurably different waveform energy, verified by src/__tests__/piano-phase2.test.ts lines 38-58 and by re-running the test suite), and Clav/Digital/Misc are honestly labeled as synthesis per spec -- but the false 'recorded' claim on the three types that are required to be recorded is a direct, hard-gate-level violation, not an ambiguous edge case.

criteria.label: Two-layer Piano behavior
evidence: src/audio/PianoLayer.ts constructs independent effectChain, levelGain, and voice maps per layer (A defaults enabled/level 8.5, B defaults disabled/level 6.0, lines 51-67).

Live test: enabling Layer B (while A stayed on) and holding a single key raised VOICES from 2 to 4, proving Layer B genuinely spawns its own voices rather than being a cosmetic toggle; disabling a layer immediately stops only that layer's voices (src/__tests__/piano-phase2.test.ts lines 108-111, reproduced live).

Octave shift is applied per-voice via config.octaveShift in PianoVoice.ts (effectiveMidi calculation, line 61); focus (star) switching confirmed live and in setFocusedLayer (PianoEngine.ts lines 261-265).
Cleanup on allNotesOff/dispose verified both by test (engine.dispose(), PianoLayer.dispose()) and live observation (voice count decayed to 0 after key release).

criteria.label: Detailed Piano controls
evidence: src/audio/PianoVoice.ts: KB Touch applies a velocity power curve (0.65/0.82/1.35 exponents, lines 72-78), Dyn Comp raises soft-stroke velocity (lines 81-84), Timbre applies distinct biquad filter types/gains per setting including Electric-only Dyno 1/Dyno 2 (configureTimbreFilter, lines 157-189), Soft Release extends release time 1.6x except for Clav (lines 401-405), Unison spawns 2-3 detuned voices per note (spawnSampleVoice/spawnClavinetVoice etc.), String Res adds a sympathetic 2nd-harmonic oscillator gated on stringRes+sustain/acoustic type (setupStringResonance, lines 122-124, 191-208).

src/__tests__/piano-phase2.test.ts piano.velocity-controls test (lines 119-178) asserts KB Touch Light > Heavy effective velocity, Dyn Comp raises soft velocity, Timbre Soft/Bright filter gain sign flips -- I re-ran this test locally and it passes.

Not rated higher because these controls are validated only through the mocked AudioContext's parameter bookkeeping (frequency.value, gain.value on Mock nodes), not through actual rendered-signal measurement, so 'measurably changes rendered audio' is demonstrated in the real app only via manual/live inspection rather than automated proof.

criteria.label: Input and fallback reliability
evidence: Sustain via UI/keyboard/MIDI CC64 works and honors SUSTPED per layer (piano-phase2.test.ts piano.pedals test, lines 180-223, verified passing; live test showed VOICES tracking correctly through key-hold/release cycles).

Fallback: sampleLibrary.setSimulateFailure(true) produces a labeled triangle-oscillator fallback voice without crashing (src/audio/PianoVoice.ts spawnFallbackVoice, lines 341-364; test piano.fallback, lines 225-252, passing).

Stuck-note prevention: PianoVoice.cleanup() disconnects all nodes and calls onEndedCallback; pruneDeadVoices() runs on every noteOn/noteOff/setSustain; verified live (voice count reliably returned to 0, no leaked voices across repeated play).

Soft pedal (una corda) is implemented (velocity/attack dampening in PianoVoice.ts lines 86-89, 109) but is optional scope per specs/nord-stage-4.piano.json and I found no UI/doc label marking it as an 'approximation' as the spec's optional-scope note requests -- a minor gap on an optional item, not a required-feature failure.

criteria.label: Shared graph and gain staging
evidence: src/audio/PianoEngine.ts setupEngineGraph (lines 114-162): single AudioContext instance, masterBus -> masterLevelGain -> masterLimiter (DynamicsCompressorNode, threshold -0.5dB/ratio 20:1/attack 1ms/release 50ms) -> ctx.destination; shared RotaryEffect sums into masterBus; both PianoLayer A and B connect effectChain.output -> levelGain -> masterBus.
PianoLayer.ts constructor (lines 69-80) gives each layer its own EffectChain and levelGain bus, satisfying 'per-layer buses'.
AudioContext is injectable via AudioEngineOptions (constructor, PianoEngine.ts line 49-56), enabling deterministic tests; confirmed by MockAudioContext-based tests all passing.
dispose() (PianoEngine.ts lines 375-396, PianoLayer.ts lines 233-241, EffectChain.ts lines 143-159) disconnects all nodes and closes the context -- verified via the node-count-based cleanup tests.

Not rated 4: the 'brickwall' limiter uses a 20:1 ratio rather than a true limiter ratio, and automation/gain-staging correctness is only verified through mock parameter bookkeeping, not real rendered-signal measurement of headroom/clipping.

criteria.label: Audible effect coverage
evidence: Code inspection of all 7 units confirms real, non-trivial Web Audio graphs, not stubs: ReverbEffect (procedurally generated convolution impulse per type/decay, dry/wet crossfade, damping filter), DelayEffect (stereo delay lines with per-repeat feedback filtering and ping-pong cross-feedback), AmpEqEffect (3-band EQ + distinct WaveShaper curves for Twin/JC/Small + LP24/HP24 cascaded biquads + To Rotary send), RotaryEffect (split horn/rotor filters, LFO-driven stereo panners with distinct accel time constants for horn vs. rotor, drive waveshaper), Mod1/Mod2/Compressor units (read but summarized) all wired with real gain/filter/oscillator nodes.

Live test confirmed audible-adjacent state changes: Reverb Type Stage->Hall, Delay bypass LED lit, Mod1 Type A-Pan->Trem, all reflected immediately in both DOM state and visual LED/label with zero console errors.

Gap: src/__tests__/effects-phase2.test.ts exercises every unit exclusively through MockAudioContext and asserts only getParams() equality (e.g. lines 104-209) -- no test renders real audio (no OfflineAudioContext, no AnalyserNode, no captured Float32Array output) to prove 'every unit and every listed type... measurably changes a standardized rendered signal' per the task's explicit audio-test rule that state-only tests with fakes are insufficient when audible behavior is claimed. The real implementation appears sound from code review and live use, but the required proof-by-test is missing.

criteria.label: Routing and control
evidence: Signal order in EffectChain.ts (lines 67-83) exactly matches the spec's requiredOrder: input -> Mod1 -> Mod2 -> Delay -> AmpEq -> Compressor -> Reverb -> (Rotary when routed) -> output.

Focus/group/global: PianoEngine.getTargetEffectChains (lines 298-308) targets focused layer by default, both layers in group or global mode; effects-phase2.test.ts routing test (lines 35-79, passing) verifies group-mode Delay tempo propagates to both layers and global mode sets both chains' global flag.

Per-unit bypass and all-effects bypass verified via EffectChain.setAllEffectsBypass (dry bypass path input->allEffectsBypassGain->output, click-free via setTargetAtTime 15ms ramp) and live-tested Delay on/off toggle.

To Rotary routing: AmpEqEffect.toRotaryOutput feeds EffectChain.routeToRotary, which connects reverb.output to the shared RotaryEffect only when routed -- correctly keeping Reverb before Rotary per spec (reverb.output -> chainOutputGain AND -> sharedRotary.input).

Delay feedback filter Off/LP/HP/BP cycling tested and passing (effects-phase2.test.ts lines 81-100); filter sits inside the feedback loop per DelayEffect.ts routing (delay->filter->feedback->delay), matching the spec's 'progressively more filtered' requirement.

Not rated 4 because, as with effectCoverage, the routing correctness is proven only against mock node connectivity/parameter state, not a real rendered-signal check that on/bypass or focus targeting actually changes final output.

criteria.label: Audible/visible feedback
evidence: Live test: Type/Reverb/Mod1 button clicks produced immediate, correctly-updated on-screen sublabels and LED states (Delay LED gained 'active' class synchronously with aria-pressed flip); voice-count status text updated in real time with key press/release.

Program OLED area is described in evidence/stage2-visual-audit.md as showing live piano type/model feedback; this was not independently exercised beyond the Type button test, so full OLED-text-sync coverage across every control is not independently confirmed.
No lag or stale-state issues were observed in the ~15 interactions performed during the live session.

criteria.label: Failure and stress behavior
evidence: Asset failure fallback tested and passing (piano.fallback, sampleLibrary.setSimulateFailure(true) -> triangle-oscillator voice, no crash).

MIDI denied path inherited and re-tested from Phase 1 (audio.test.ts lines 121-133: MidiController with null access reports 'denied' status without throwing); live capture's status bar also showed 'MIDI: DENIED' cleanly (expected in a headless/sandboxed browser without a granted MIDI permission, not a code defect).
Voice stealing under max polyphony (32) is inherited/tested (audio.test.ts lines 170-190).

No explicit test or live exercise of rapid effect-parameter churn, simultaneous multi-layer + multi-effect stress, or focus-loss-during-playback recovery, so this criterion is not proven at the highest level despite no observed failures in the interactions performed.

criteria.label: Audio architecture
evidence: Clear boundary separation: SampleLibrary (source generation/lookup), PianoVoice (per-note DSP graph), PianoLayer (voice pool + bus + effect chain), PianoEngine (global routing/focus/master path), EffectChain + 7 discrete effect unit classes (one file each) -- a maintainable, extensible structure for Phase 3 to build on (e.g. Organ/Synth could reuse EffectChain/RotaryEffect).
AudioContext is injected via constructor option (AudioEngineOptions), enabling the whole test suite to run deterministically against MockAudioContext without real audio hardware.

Some architectural smell: PianoVoice.ts (481 lines) concentrates velocity-curve, timbre, string-resonance, and 4 separate instrument-synthesis code paths in one class, which will grow further once Organ/Synth engines are added in Phase 3.

criteria.label: Real-boundary tests
evidence: All 6 test files use MockAudioContext (src/__tests__/audio-mock.ts), whose Mock nodes (MockGainNode, MockBiquadFilterNode, MockConvolverNode, etc.) only record connections and parameter values -- none of them perform actual signal processing, so no test in the suite renders or measures real audio output.

effects-phase2.test.ts (the primary Phase 2 effects test file) exclusively asserts getParams() equality after calling updateParams() -- e.g. 'expect(mod1.getParams().type).toBe(type)' -- which only proves a setter/getter round-trip, not that the signal is processed or altered, directly conflicting with inputs/TASK.md's audio test rules: 'When behavior is claimed audible, a state-only test with fakes is not enough' and specs/nord-stage-4.effects.json acceptance: 'a label, enum, or disconnected node is not an effect.'

The one partial exception is piano-phase2.test.ts's instrument-library test (lines 38-58), which does compare real Float32Array sample data (grandL vs uprightL vs electricL) generated by the actual production synthesis functions -- a genuine real-boundary numeric check, though it is testing procedurally-generated buffers mislabeled as recordings (see instrumentBreadth).

No OfflineAudioContext rendering, no AnalyserNode-based spectral/level assertions, and no 'silence vs. non-silence' or 'effect on vs. bypass measurably differs' assertions exist anywhere in the suite, despite the app itself (per live testing and code review) appearing to genuinely process audio correctly. This is a significant gap between what is claimed/implemented and what is proven by the test suite.

criteria.label: Performance and maintainability
evidence: All 6 inherited Phase 1 tests remain present and passing alongside 3 new Phase 2 test files (piano-phase2.test.ts, effects-phase2.test.ts), matching tests/feature-matrix.json's regression.phase1 entry; I independently reran `pnpm run test` (33/33 passing), `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, and `pnpm run build`, all clean with zero warnings.

Cleanup discipline is consistent across every class (dispose()/cleanup() methods disconnect all nodes, clear listeners, stop oscillators) and was empirically verified live (voice counts reliably return to 0, no console errors accumulate over ~15 interactions).

Effect unit classes follow a consistent, repeated structural pattern (input/output/dry/wet/setParams/getParams/dispose) which aids readability but also means the six effect files duplicate a fair amount of bypass/dry-wet-ramp boilerplate that could be factored into a shared base class.

Naming is mostly clear, but function names like synthesizeAcousticGrandBuffer alongside docstrings/state labels claiming 'recorded' sample sets are actively misleading to a maintainer, which is a real maintainability and trust cost tied to the instrumentBreadth finding above.

issues: Critical honesty-contract violation (Phase 2 hard gate): IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json and IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md declare Grand/Upright/Electric as bundled recorded sample sets with fabricated sources, licenses, and a 27-file manifest (audio/samples/*.pcm) that does not exist in the artifact; src/audio/SampleLibrary.ts shows all three are 100% procedurally synthesized at runtime. This directly triggers the rubric's 'Generated buffers presented as recordings score 0' rule for pianoLibrary.instrumentBreadth.

Effects Phase 2 tests (src/__tests__/effects-phase2.test.ts) are state-only tests against a fully mocked AudioContext (no real signal rendering/measurement), which conflicts with the task's explicit rule that state-only tests with fakes are insufficient for claimed audible behavior.

Minor: the Piano TYPE button's accessible name does not include the currently selected type (unlike every other TYPE-style button in the app), so screen-reader users cannot tell which piano type is active from the control's name alone.

Minor: soft pedal (una corda) approximation is implemented but not labeled as an approximation anywhere in the UI or docs, as requested by the piano spec's optional-scope note (not a required-feature failure, but a missed extra-credit condition).

Positive: technical gates all pass cleanly on independent re-run (test 33/33, typecheck, lint, build), and the live built app (dist/) was manually exercised via Playwright with zero functional console errors, correct voice-count behavior for single/multi-layer/multi-key play, and correctly-reflected effect/layer state changes.
